rationale: Evidence across multiple cohort studies and clinical reports confirms that biallelic pathogenic variants in CLN3 cause a spectrum ranging from severe juvenile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (JNCL/Batten disease) to isolated, non-syndromic rod-cone dystrophy (RP101, OMIM #621548). Classic JNCL manifests in childhood (onset 3-7 years) with rapid central visual decline followed invariably by progressive dementia, epilepsy/seizures (HP:0001250), motor decline, and premature mortality by the second to third decade. In contrast, patients with RP101 exhibit retinal disease (early-onset or late-onset rod-cone dystrophy) with prolonged preservation of general neurological and cognitive function (HP:0100543) well into adulthood (persisting into their 40s to 70s). Because the ocular features of RP101 (pigmentary retinopathy, macular atrophy, attenuated retinal vessels, and electronegative or unrecordable ERGs) overlap completely with typical autosomal recessive nonsyndromic retinitis pigmentosa, differentiation from other non-syndromic RP genes is not possible on clinical retinal examination alone and requires next-generation sequencing panels.

evidence.text: In a French inherited retinal disorder cohort, 15 patients from 11 unrelated families with biallelic CLN3 mutations presented with nonsyndromic retinal degeneration, characterized by two rod-cone dystrophy patterns (mild middle-age onset reaching legal blindness in their 70s, and severe early macular atrophic changes reaching legal blindness in their 40s) without classic JNCL neurodegeneration.

source.title: Retinal Phenotype of Patients With Isolated Retinal Degeneration Due to CLN3 Pathogenic Variants in a French Retinitis Pigmentosa Cohort
source.quote: A total of 15 cases from 11 unrelated families harboring biallelic CLN3 variants were identified. All patients presented with nonsyndromic IRD. Two distinct patterns of retinal disease could be identified: a mild rod-cone degeneration of middle-age onset (n = 6; legal blindness threshold reached by 70s) and a severe retinal degeneration with early macular atrophic changes (n = 9; legal blindness threshold reached by 40s).

evidence.text: Classic JNCL presents with early rapid visual loss, bull's-eye maculopathy, and early systemic neurocognitive deterioration with cognitive or neurologic signs present in 75% at the time of diagnosis (mean diagnosis age 8.3 years), along with systemic markers like vacuolated lymphocytes.

source.title: Juvenile Batten Disease (CLN3): Detailed Ocular Phenotype, Novel Observations, Clinical Algorithm, and Recommendations for Clinical Trials
source.quote: Age of onset ranged from 3 to 7 years (mean, 5.3 years). The age at diagnosis of JNCL ranged from 7 to 10 years (mean, 8.3 years). Six children displayed eccentric fixation, and 6 children had cognitive or neurologic signs at the time of diagnosis (75%).

evidence.text: Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis variants display phenotypic divergence ranging from severe neurocognitive regression and seizures (67%) to isolated nonsyndromic retinal dystrophies (17%), highlighting that genetic testing is required to distinguish underlying molecular drivers.

source.title: Genetic reasons for phenotypic diversity in neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses and high-resolution imaging as a marker of retinal disease
source.quote: Subjects presented with varying phenotypes ranging from severe neurocognitive features (n = 8; 67%), including seizures and developmental delays and regressions, to nonsyndromic retinal dystrophies (n = 2; 17%).

evidence.text: Biallelic variants across CLN genes demonstrate significant phenotypic pleiotropy, making definitive clinical distinction and allele-phenotype correlations challenging without comprehensive genetic sequencing.

source.title: Phenotypic Variability of Retinal Disease Among a Cohort of Patients with Biallelic Variants in CLN Genes
source.quote: Substantial phenotypic variability among variants in the CLN genes makes identification of genotype-phenotype or allele-phenotype correlations challenging.

new_directions.question_text: Do peripheral blood smears for vacuolated lymphocytes or electron microscopy of inclusions consistently yield negative findings in patients with RP101 compared to classic CLN3 Batten disease?
new_directions.rationale: Classic CLN3 disease shows 100% vacuolated lymphocytes in peripheral blood films; determining if RP101 patients completely lack these lysosomal inclusions would provide an accessible systemic biomarker before genetic test turnaround.

new_directions.question_text: What specific CLN3 residual protein activity or alternative splicing thresholds differentiate retina-restricted rod-cone dystrophy from neurodegenerative JNCL?
new_directions.rationale: Elucidating the biochemical threshold that spares cortical neurons while failing photoreceptors/RPE will clarify the mechanism of tissue-specific vulnerability in RP101.
